metadata.title: Embodied Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Manipulation Planning With Embodied World Model
metadata.abstract_summary: Plans robot manipulation by searching a tree of discrete action skills, branching from priors and reflecting on failed branches, with parallel search across simulated worlds.

sections.heading: Claims
sections.text:
What the paper proposes or defines, as extracted (section, page):
- **Discrete action skills set** (category B) - Standardizes agent task plans as five discrete semantic action primitives, each backed by a dedicated API, so a VLM can structure executable action sequences. (section III. A. Action Skills Set, p. 3)
  > we model robot skills as a set of discrete semantic action primitives.
- **Priori Branching** (category C) - Generates diverse candidate plan branches from semantic and spatial scene analysis before execution, forming the initial planning tree. (section III. C. 1) Priori Branching, p. 4)
  > The model is encouraged to explicitly branch at decision points where multiple feasible action choices exist.
- **Reflective Branching** (category C) - Diagnoses simulated execution failures and expands the planning tree with corrective branches instead of committing to a failing plan. (section III. C. 2) Tree Searching and Reﬂective Branching, p. 4)
  > Reﬂective Branching analyzes simulated execution outcomes, identiﬁes failure causes, and dynamically generates revised branches during the tree search process.
- **BFS planning-tree search (Algorithm 1)** (category C) - Searches the world-model-grounded planning tree breadth-first, evaluating each node action in simulation and returning the shortest feasible root-to-leaf plan. (section III. C. 2) Tree Searching and Reﬂective Branching, p. 4)

sections.heading: Method
sections.text:
- **Discrete action skills set**: Primitives: [PICK UP, obj], [PUT ON, surface], [PUT INTO, container], [OPEN, obj], [CLOSE, obj]; PICK UP uses AnyGrasp pose estimation; OPEN/CLOSE use scripted primitives; optional [PICK UP, obj] (POSE) disambiguates grasps.
- **Priori Branching**: VLM parses object instances, relational predicates and articulation states, then emits branches at decision points: instance-level branching (object choice) and manipulation-parameter branching (grasp configuration); shared action prefixes are merged into a compact tree.
- **Reflective Branching**: VLM compares object states before/after simulated execution; unsafe if changes cannot be recovered with available skills. Corrections: relocate collision-affected objects before retrying, or reorder conflicting actions; failed subtrees are removed and revised branches merged.
- **BFS planning-tree search (Algorithm 1)**: T ←PrioriBranching(I, t); Q ←[T.root.children]; loop: N ←Q.pop(), I ←S.execute(N.A), R ←VLMJudge(N.A, I); success pushes children or returns extractPath(N); failure calls extractPaths(N), T.removeSubtree(N), merges reﬂective branches and queues nnew.
- **Multi-world parallelism**: Newly generated child nodes are rolled out in parallel from their parent terminal states; BFS depth equals high-level action count, so same-parent rollouts run concurrently without violating causal structure.
- **Task success rate metric**: Success rate = proportion of trials that achieve the speciﬁed goal without causing harmful changes to the environment; each task repeated for 30 independent trials; failure modes also broken into execution, depth, and world-model planning errors.

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- Evidence the authors report:
  - Discrete action skills set: Seven real-world tabletop tasks on an xArm6 with 30 independent trials per task; skills executed end-to-end via API implementations.
  - Priori Branching: Ablation shows removing Priori Branching yields a single-branch tree and wrong decisions on multi-path Tasks 2, 5, 7.
  - Reflective Branching: Ablation without Reflective Branching drops overall success to 32.08%; module accuracy measured at 98.75%.
  - BFS planning-tree search (Algorithm 1): Algorithm 1 evaluated on seven tasks plus a disturbance task, 30 trials each; highest success on every task, average 80.42%.
  - Multi-world parallelism: Task 5 simulation time reduced from 55 s to 26 s with parallel rollouts.
  - Task success rate metric: Seven tasks plus disturbance task, 30 trials each; EToT averages 80.42% versus lower baselines, with failure analysis percentages reported.
- Limitations the authors state:
  - Discrete action skills set: OPEN and CLOSE rely on manually scripted control primitives; most actions do not model multiple candidate poses.
  - Priori Branching: Initial branches may be invalid or unsafe due to incomplete physical reasoning.
  - Reflective Branching: Reﬂective Branching errors occur on Task 7; diagnosis depends on simulated rollout fidelity.
  - BFS planning-tree search (Algorithm 1): Tree-based planning becomes increasingly expensive as the search depth and branching factor grow.
  - Multi-world parallelism: Parallelism applies to same-parent children; overall cost remains high at 13341.63 tokens and 153.00 s per task on average.
- Limitations they do not state: not assessed. Results are the authors' own, from their simulations, benchmarks or surveys; none evaluates delegation to cheaper models on software work.
